segments: And he mentioned,
another [narrator] before him, from ʿUmārah ibn Ghaziyyah,
from Abū az-Zubayr,
from Jābir ibn ʿAbdullāh,

who said: On the day of Uhud, when the people turned back, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at one side with twelve men of the Anṣār, among them Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydullāh. The polytheists caught up with them, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned and said, "Who will [face] the enemy?"
Ṭalḥah said, "I will."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Stay where you are."
A man of the Anṣār said, "I will, O Messenger of Allah." He said, "You."
So he fought until he was killed. Then [the Prophet ﷺ] turned and saw the polytheists, and said, "Who will [face] the enemy?"
Ṭalḥah said, "I will." He said, "Stay where you are."
A man of the Anṣār said, "I will." He said, "You."

So he fought until he was killed. He kept saying this, and a man of the Anṣār would go out to them and fight as fiercely as those before him until he was killed, until only the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Ṭalḥah ibn ʿUbaydullāh remained. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Who will [face] the enemy?"
Ṭalḥah said, "I will."
So Ṭalḥah fought the fight of the eleven, until his hand was struck and his fingers were cut off, and he said, "Ḥass!"
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said,
"Had you said 'Bismillāh,' the angels would have lifted you up while the people looked on."
Then Allah drove the polytheists back.
And ʿAmr al-Nāqid,
all of them from al-Qāsim ibn Mālik,
ʿAmr said: Qāsim ibn Mālik al-Muzanī narrated to us,
Ayyūb ibn ʿĀʾidh al-Ṭāʾī narrated to us,
from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujāhid,
from Ibn ʿAbbās,
who said: Allah made the prayer obligatory through the tongue of your Prophet ﷺ as two rakʿahs for the traveller, four for the resident, and one rakʿah in [times of] fear.

He used to say: Ḥudhayfah ibn al-Yamān said: By Allah, I am the most knowledgeable of people about every trial that will occur between me and the Hour. It is only that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not confide something to me about that which he told no one else, but the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was speaking in a gathering in which I was present about trials, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while enumerating the trials, said:
"Among them are three that will hardly leave anything, and among them are trials like the summer winds, some small and some great."
Ḥudhayfah said: All of those men have gone except me.
U6-07486.error: Mistranslated 'wa mā bī illā an yakūna... asarra ilayya' — the sense is 'it is not because the Messenger ﷺ confided something to me that he told no one else'; the English as written reads ambiguously, and the first clause is rendered as a negated confidence. Corrected to make the meaning clear.

segments: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ that the left side of the mosque had been left empty. So the Prophet ﷺ said:
"Whoever populates the left side of the mosque will have written for him a double share of reward."
U6-11994.error: Minor: 'ʿammara' means to populate/attend and keep it occupied, not merely fill.

segments: The last glance I took at the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was when the curtain was lifted on Monday. I looked at his face, as if it were a page of the Qurʾān, while the people were behind Abū Bakr in prayer. [Abū Bakr] wanted to move, but he ﷺ signaled to him to stay in place, and he let the curtain fall. He died at the end of that day.
U6-02604.error: Wrong subject: it was Abū Bakr who wanted to move back and the Prophet ﷺ who signaled him and dropped the curtain, not Abū Bakr being signaled.

segments: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood on the day of al-Aḍḥā and said: "
Whoever faces our qiblah, prays our prayer, and performs our rite of sacrifice, let him not slaughter until he has prayed."
Then my maternal uncle stood up and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I hastened my sacrifice in order to feed my family and the people of my household," or he said, "my family and my neighbors."
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "
Slaughter another animal."
He said: "I have a milk-fed young female goat that is dearer to me than two sheep for meat." He said: "
Slaughter it, for it is the better of your two sacrifices. But a jadhaʿah will not suffice on behalf of anyone after you."

Three men came to the houses of the wives of the Prophet ﷺ asking about the worship of the Prophet ﷺ. When they were told, it was as though they considered it little, and they said, "Where are we compared to the Prophet ﷺ? Allah has forgiven him his earlier and later sins."
One of them said, "As for me, I will pray all night, always."
Another said, "I will fast all the time and never break my fast."
Another said, "I will keep away from women and never marry."
Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came and said:
"You are the ones who said such and such. By Allah, I am the one among you who fears Allah most and is most mindful of Him,
yet I fast and I break my fast,
I pray and I sleep, and I marry women.
So whoever turns away from my Sunnah is not of me."
U6-01832.error: Segment 3: الدهر means all the time (perpetually); 'continuously' is imprecise but not an error. No change in meaning found.

segments: Whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr, and whoever takes a handspan of land unjustly will have it hung around his neck on the Day of Resurrection from seven earths."
Ḥātim ibn Siyāh al-Marwazī added in this hadith: Maʿmar said: It reached me from az-Zuhrī, and I did not hear it from him, that he added in this hadith:
"Whoever is killed defending his property is a martyr."
Shuʿayb ibn Abī Ḥamzah likewise narrated this hadith from az-Zuhrī, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbdillāh, from ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Sahl, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, from the Prophet ﷺ.
Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah narrated it from az-Zuhrī, from Ṭalḥah ibn ʿAbdillāh, from Saʿīd ibn Zayd, from the Prophet ﷺ, and Sufyān did not mention ʿAbd ar-Raḥmān ibn ʿAmr ibn Sahl in it.
This is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ hadith.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ came out while we were in the Ṣuffah, and said:
"Which of you would like to go out every morning to Buṭḥān or to al-ʿAqīq and return from it with two large-humped she-camels, without any sin and without severing family ties?"
We said, "O Messenger of Allah, we would like that." He said:

"Then does not one of you go out in the morning to the mosque and learn, or recite, two verses from the Book of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic? That is better for him than two she-camels; three verses are better for him than three, and four are better for him than four, and than their number in camels."
[The wife] of the Prophet ﷺ [reported] that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw a girl in the house of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, with a dark mark on her face, and he said:
"She is under the effect of the evil eye, so seek ruqyah for her."
Meaning, there was a yellowish pallor on her face.
[It was] read to him while I listened,
from Ibn al-Qāsim,
who said: Mālik narrated to me,
from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father,
from Jābir ibn ʿAbd Allāh,

may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when he came down from Ṣafā, would walk until, when his feet descended into the bottom of the valley, he would run until he came out of it.
